::: {#sol-three-vertices}

Five, drawn in @fig-three-vertices.
The root is one of the three vertices,
so the left and right binary trees have two vertices between them:
2 and 0, 1 and 1, or 0 and 2.
There is one binary tree with no vertices, the empty one,
and one with one vertex, a root with two empty binary trees.
There are two with two vertices: a root with one vertex in its left binary tree, or in its right one.
So there are $2 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 2 = 5$ binary trees with three vertices.

::: {#fig-three-vertices}

The first goes down to the left twice.
The second goes down to the left and then to the right.
The third has a root with one point below it to the left and one below it to the right.
The fourth goes down to the right and then to the left.
The fifth goes down to the right twice." width="75%"}

The five binary trees with three vertices.
